key_insight: CS3F is a training-free, zero-shot method that repurposes frozen 2D foundation models to localize anomalies in 3D medical volumes by comparing volumetric tokens across subjects.
clinical_relevance: This could help flag unusual findings in scans where labeled training data are scarce, across changing protocols and diseases.
method: Decompose each 3D scan along multiple axes and encode slices with a 2D vision transformer.
Pool neighboring slice features into localized volumetric tokens.
Score anomalies by cross-subject mutual similarity, then use coarse-to-fine tokenization for finer localization.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated on brain MRI for metastases, glioma, and stroke, and also tested on lung CT for broader generalizability.
watch_item: Performance depends on lesion contrast and modality, and depth pooling can weaken small focal lesion signals.
paper_title: Toward Training-Free Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection in 3D Medical Images: A Batch-Based Approach Using 2D Foundation Models
